actions.action: Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots
If rot, trim mushy roots and repot in fresh chunky mix (soil plus perlite or bark) in a pot with good drainage
If roots fine, clear the drainage holes
Make sure the pot doesn't sit in water or a saucer
Check soil with finger or skewer before watering, letting top 2-3 cm dry
Move plant to the brightest spot, e.g. south or west window
Add a grow light during cloudy stretches
Post a photo of the whole plant and root ball

reason: The answer diagnoses overwatering and root rot when the plant was actually underwatered. Its advice to water less, let the soil dry, and possibly trim roots and repot is the opposite of the needed thorough soaking and would likely delay recovery.
